description: BPSC TRE Computer Science Model Test Paper 03 (English Medium) containing 120 questions across General Studies and Computer Science.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the value of (x + 1/x)^2?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Expanding (x + 1/x)^2 gives x^2 + 2 + 1/x^2, which is not present in options A, B, or C[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: An article is marked at 10% more than the CP. If a discount of 10% is allowed, which of the following is correct?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Net percentage change = +10 - 10 - (10 * 10) / 100 = -1%, which represents a 1% loss[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: By what least number should 81 be divided to obtain a perfect cube?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 81 divided by 3 gives 27, which is a perfect cube (3^3 = 27)[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: The difference between two whole numbers is 66 and their ratio is 2:5. What are the two numbers?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Let the numbers be 2x and 5x. 5x - 2x = 3x = 66 => x = 22. Numbers are 2 * 22 = 44 and 5 * 22 = 110[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: In a parallelogram ABCD, angle A and angle B are in the ratio 1:2. Find the measure of angle A.
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles in a parallelogram are supplementary: x + 2x = 180 degrees => 3x = 180 degrees => x = 60 degrees[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: The total surface area of a cylinder is 968 cm^2 and its radius is 7 cm. What is the height of the cylinder?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: If (-3)^(m+1) * (-3)^5 = (-3)^7, then what is the value of m?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Equating the powers on base (-3): (m + 1) + 5 = 7 => m + 6 = 7 => m = 1[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: If variables x and y are inversely proportional, then which of the following relations holds true?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: When x and y are in inverse proportion, their product x * y remains constant[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: A piece of uniform wire of resistance R is cut into 5 equal parts. If these parts are connected in parallel and their equivalent resistance is R prime, what is the ratio R/R prime?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Resistance of each part = R/5. In parallel, 1/R' = 5 / (R/5) = 25/R => R/R' = 25[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become 4 times itself at the same rate?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: SI for doubling = P in 5 years => Rate = 20%. To become 4 times, required SI = 3P => Time = 3 * 5 = 15 years.

questions.questionText: If 30th April is Tuesday, what day of the week will be 10th May of the same year?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: April has 30 days. Number of days to 10th May = 10. 10 mod 7 = 3 days after Tuesday = Friday, which is not listed[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: The human eye forms the real and inverted image of an object at its:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The crystalline lens of the human eye focuses incoming light rays to form a real and inverted image on the retina[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: In angiospermic plants, which reproductive part produces pollen grains?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The anther is the male reproductive organ of the flower that contains microsporangia where pollen grains develop[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which functional process is mainly utilized in commercial production of green hydrogen from water?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Green hydrogen is generated through the electrolysis of water powered by renewable electricity sources[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which planet in our solar system exhibits a cratered surface most resembling Earth's Moon?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Mercury lacks an atmosphere and has an ancient, heavily cratered terrain visually very similar to the Moon[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: On the basis of hominid fossil discoveries, which geographical zone is considered the primary cradle of human origin?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The East African Rift Valley has yielded early hominid fossils, marking it as the primary cradle of human origin[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: In Indian settlement geography, dry point settlements are commonly located in:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Dry point settlements are built on upland patches in low-lying, flood-prone river regions to avoid inundation[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: In which district of Bihar is the production of paddy crop recorded as the highest?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Rohtas is the leading paddy-producing district in Bihar and is often referred to as the rice bowl of the state[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: The capital city of Iran, Tehran, is located at the foot of which mountain range?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Tehran is situated on the southern slopes of the Alborz (Alburz) mountain range in northern Iran[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Who was the Viceroy of British India during the tragic Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Lord Chelmsford served as the Viceroy of India from 1916 to 1921 during the Jallianwala Bagh massacre[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Who presided as the first President over the inaugural session of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress held in Bombay in 1885[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Who among the following nationalist leaders was widely revered as the 'Grand Old Man of India'?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji was revered as the Grand Old Man of India for his contribution to the national freedom movement[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which national movement was launched under Mahatma Gandhi's call of 'Do or Die' in August 1942?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi gave the mantra 'Do or Die' at the Gowalia Tank Maidan during the launch of the Quit India Movement in 1942[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: The historic Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was led by:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Vallabhbhai Patel successfully led the Bardoli peasant movement against land revenue hikes, earning the title 'Sardar'[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Who among the following was not an active organizer of the Home Rule League Movement in India?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The two Home Rule Leagues were initiated by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant in 1916[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: The All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) was established at Lucknow in 1936 under the presidency of:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was elected as the first President of the All India Kisan Sabha at Lucknow in 1936[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Who invited Mahatma Gandhi to visit Champaran in 1917 to look into the grievances of indigo farmers?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Raj Kumar Shukla persistently pursued Mahatma Gandhi and convinced him to visit Champaran to witness the indigo ryots' plight[cite: 1, 2].

questions.questionText: In which year was the state of Bihar separated from the Bengal Presidency?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Bihar and Orissa were carved out from the Bengal Presidency into a separate province on 22 March 1912.

questions.questionText: The Someshwar fort and hilly range in Bihar are situated in which district?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Someshwar range forms the outer foothills of the Himalayas in the northern part of West Champaran district.

questions.questionText: Which river is traditionally notorious as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to frequent floods and changing courses?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Kosi river is called the Sorrow of Bihar because of catastrophic floods and avulsion across the north Bihar plains.

questions.questionText: Valmiki National Park, the only national park in Bihar, is located in:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Valmiki National Park is situated in the West Champaran district of Bihar on the border with Nepal.

questions.questionText: The process of separating lighter husk from heavier grain seeds using wind currents is called:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Winnowing separates lighter husk and chaff from heavier grains by letting the mixture fall in moving wind.

questions.questionText: Which metal is extracted commercially from its primary ore, Bauxite?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Aluminium is commercially produced by refining and smelting its primary ore, bauxite.

questions.questionText: Which gas protects life on Earth by absorbing hazardous ultraviolet solar radiations in the stratosphere?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The ozone layer (O3) in the stratosphere absorbs harmful high-frequency ultraviolet radiation from the Sun[cite: 2].

questions.questionText: The fundamental structural and functional unit of the human kidney is known as:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The nephron is the basic structural and functional filtration unit of the human kidney.

questions.questionText: An electric generator operates on which scientific phenomenon discovered by Michael Faraday?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Electric generators convert mechanical energy into electrical energy based on Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction.

questions.questionText: What is the value of acceleration due to gravity (g) at the center of the Earth?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: At the Earth's center, the net gravitational attraction from all directions cancels out, resulting in g = 0.

questions.questionText: Which endocrine gland in the human body regulates blood glucose levels by secreting insulin?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The endocrine portion of the pancreas (beta cells of Islets of Langerhans) secretes the hormone insulin.

questions.questionText: The permanent hardness of water is primarily caused by dissolved salts of:
questions.optionB: Chlorides and sulfates of calcium and magnesium
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Permanent hardness is caused by dissolved calcium and magnesium chlorides and sulfates, which cannot be removed by boiling.

questions.questionText: Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly that drafted the Constitution of India?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the permanent elected President of the Constituent Assembly of India[cite: 1, 2, 3].

questions.questionText: Any combinational digital circuit can be constructed solely using repeated interconnections of:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Both NAND and NOR are universal gates; any Boolean function can be implemented using either gate alone[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: How many total output rows are present in the truth table of a 4-input OR gate?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A truth table for n binary inputs has 2^n rows. With 4 inputs, there are 2^4 = 16 rows[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: In digital electronics, a negative edge-triggered flip-flop changes its internal state:
questions.optionA: During the transition of the clock signal from High to Low (1 to 0)
questions.optionB: Whenever the clock level is continuously Low
questions.optionC: During the transition of clock from Low to High
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Negative edge-triggered flip-flops sample their inputs and toggle states on the falling edge (High-to-Low) of the clock pulse[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What is the binary result of the bitwise operation (1010 AND 1100)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Bitwise AND operation: 1 AND 1 = 1; 0 AND 1 = 0; 1 AND 0 = 0; 0 AND 0 = 0. Output is 1000[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What are the two distinct output signals produced by an arithmetic half-adder circuit?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A half-adder adds two single binary bits and produces two outputs: Sum (A XOR B) and Carry (A AND B)[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is classified as non-volatile semiconductor memory?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: PROM, EPROM, and EEPROM are all non-volatile forms of Read-Only Memory that retain stored data without power[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What does the acronym PLA stand for in digital integrated circuit design?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: PLA stands for Programmable Logic Array, featuring programmable AND and programmable OR arrays[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: How many selection input lines are required to select inputs in an 8-to-1 multiplexer?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: For 2^n inputs, n select lines are needed. 2^3 = 8, so exactly 3 selection lines are required[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What is the decimal value 1234 when converted to binary, octal, and hexadecimal bases?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 1234 in binary is 10011010010; in octal is 2322; and in hexadecimal is 4D2 (since 4*256 + 13*16 + 2 = 1234)[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What is Booth's multiplication algorithm primarily used for in computer arithmetic?
questions.optionB: Multiplication of signed binary integers in two's complement form
questions.optionC: High speed binary square root extraction
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Booth's algorithm multiplies signed integers in 2's complement notation by encoding adjacent bits[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: In binary-coded decimal (BCD), how many binary bits are used to represent a single decimal digit?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In 8421 BCD encoding, each decimal digit from 0 to 9 is represented as a unique 4-bit binary nibble.

questions.questionText: In Karnaugh Maps (K-maps), what is the primary role of the 'Don't Care' (X) condition?
questions.optionB: To be utilized as either 0 or 1 to achieve larger grouping and simpler Boolean expressions
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Don't Care conditions are set to 1 or 0 as needed to form larger groupings in K-maps to minimize logic gates[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is classified as a non-linear data structure?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Graphs and trees are non-linear data structures because their elements are not organized in sequential order[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which data structure provides expected O(1) average time complexity for insertion, deletion, and searching?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Hash Tables achieve expected O(1) time complexity for search, insert, and delete through efficient hashing[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: In a standard Binary Search Tree (BST), elements stored in the left subtree of node X must be:
questions.optionA: Strictly less than the key value of node X
questions.optionB: Strictly greater than the key value of node X
questions.optionC: Equal to the key value of node X
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In a binary search tree, all keys in the left subtree of a node must be less than the node's key[cite: 1, 3].

questions.questionText: What is the numerical result of evaluating the postfix expression: 10 5 + 60 6 / * 8 - ?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: In an AVL self-balancing tree, the balance factor of any node must strictly be within:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: An AVL tree maintains height balance such that the difference between left and right subtree heights is -1, 0, or +1[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What is the average time complexity of performing binary search on a sorted array of N elements?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Binary search divides the search space in half during each step, resulting in O(log N) time[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: If the preorder traversal of a Binary Search Tree is 15, 10, 12, 11, 20, 18, 16, 19, what will be its postorder traversal?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sorting keys gives inorder (10, 11, 12, 15, 16, 18, 19, 20). Reconstructing the tree and visiting Left-Right-Root yields 11, 12, 10, 16, 19, 18, 20, 15[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: How many structurally distinct Binary Search Trees can be created out of 4 distinct keys?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The number of distinct BSTs with n keys is given by Catalan number C_n = (2n)! / ((n+1)! * n!). For n = 4, C_4 = 14[cite: 3].

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The sizeof operator evaluates types at compile time and does not execute the inner assignment, so sizeof yields 4 and k remains 15[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Big-O notation in algorithm analysis is mathematically used to represent:
questions.optionA: The asymptotic upper bound of time complexity
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Big-O notation describes an asymptotic upper bound on the growth rate of an algorithm's execution time[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which algorithmic paradigm divides a problem into subproblems, solves subproblems recursively, and combines results?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Divide and Conquer divides the problem into subproblems, conquers them recursively, and combines the results[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: How many edges does a spanning tree of a graph with N vertices have?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A spanning tree on N vertices is a connected acyclic graph and must have exactly N - 1 edges[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a graph traversal algorithm?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Greedy, Divide and Conquer, and Dynamic Programming are general algorithm design paradigms, not specific graph traversal methods like BFS or DFS[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT an NP-Complete problem?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Single-source shortest path problems can be solved in polynomial time (e.g., Dijkstra's algorithm) and are not NP-complete[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a type of operating system?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Real-time OS, Embedded OS, and Network OS are all legitimate categories of operating systems[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a memory management technique used by operating systems?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Fragmentation is an undesirable phenomenon/problem in memory allocation, not a management technique[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: In a virtual memory system, what is a page in paging?
questions.optionA: A fixed-size block of virtual memory
questions.optionB: A fixed-size block of physical memory
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A page is a contiguous, fixed-size unit of virtual memory; corresponding physical blocks are called frames[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: In a system with a page size of 4 KB and a physical address space of 64 GB, what is the number of bits required for the page offset?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Page size is 4 KB = 4096 bytes = 2^12 bytes. Therefore, 12 bits are needed to address bytes within a page[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What is a segment base in segmentation?
questions.optionA: The starting address of a segment in physical memory
questions.optionB: The starting address of a segment in virtual memory
questions.optionC: The ending address of a segment in physical memory
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In segmentation, the base register specifies the physical starting memory address where the segment is stored[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What causes thrashing to occur?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Thrashing occurs when the system spends more time executing page swaps than actual process instructions due to insufficient allocated frames[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: How is the TLB typically organized?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Translation Lookaside Buffers (TLBs) are built as either fully associative or set-associative hardware caches[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Consider a disk queue with requests for I/O to blocks on cylinders: 98 183 37 122 14 124 65 67. Considering FCFS scheduling, what is the total number of head movements if the disk head is initially at 53?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: Thread shares with other threads belonging to the same process its:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Threads in the same process share their virtual address space including the code and data segments and open files[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: In a relational database, what is a primary key?
questions.optionA: A key used to uniquely identify each record in a table
questions.optionB: A key used to establish relationships between tables
questions.optionC: A key used to sort records in a table
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A primary key is a column or set of columns chosen to uniquely identify every row in a database table[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which normal form ensures that every non-prime attribute in a table is fully functionally dependent on the primary key?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Second Normal Form (2NF) requires that no non-prime attribute is partially dependent on any candidate key[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which SQL command is used to add new rows to a database table?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The INSERT (or INSERT INTO) statement adds new records to an existing table in SQL[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: In the OSI model, which layer is responsible for routing and forwarding data packets?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Packet routing and forwarding is performed by the Network Layer, which is not listed in options A, B, or C[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which device is used to connect multiple devices within the same local area network (LAN)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A network switch operates at Layer 2 to connect workstations and devices within the same local network[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which protocol is used to send email over the Internet?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is the standard application protocol for dispatching emails across the internet[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a subnet mask in TCP/IP networking?
questions.optionA: To identify the network portion of an IP address
questions.optionB: To identify the host portion of an IP address
questions.optionC: To convert IP addresses into domain names
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A subnet mask separates the IP address into the network prefix and the host identifier portion[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What is the maximum data rate of Bluetooth version 5.0?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Bluetooth 5.0 provides an enhanced physical data transfer rate of up to 2 Mbps[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a software development life cycle model?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Waterfall, Agile, and Spiral models are all recognized SDLC methodologies[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What is the main difference between verification and validation in software testing?
questions.optionA: Verification ensures that the software is bug-free, while validation ensures that it meets the requirements.
questions.optionB: Verification is done before coding, while validation is done after coding.
questions.optionC: Verification checks if the software is built right, while validation checks if the right software is built.
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Verification ensures conformance to specifications; validation confirms the software meets actual customer needs[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a software prototype?
questions.optionA: To serve as the final version of the software
questions.optionC: To speed up the software development process
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A software prototype is built primarily to evaluate, clarify, and validate user requirements early in development[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a pillar of OOP?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Inheritance, Encapsulation, Abstraction, and Polymorphism are the core pillars of Object-Oriented Programming[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used in Java to implement inheritance?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In Java, the `extends` keyword is used when a subclass derives from a superclass[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of HTML in a web application?
questions.optionA: To define the structure of web pages
questions.optionC: To add interactivity to web pages
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: HTML defines the structural markup and document content of web pages[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a server-side scripting language commonly used in web applications?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: HTML and CSS are frontend styling/markup tools, and standard server-side scripting languages include PHP, Node.js, and Python[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: What is the computational complexity of the halting problem?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The halting problem was proven by Alan Turing to be undecidable (not computable by any Turing machine)[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a component of a Turing machine?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A standard Turing machine uses a single infinite tape for both input and output rather than a separate output tape[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an IoT protocol used for device communication?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) is a lightweight publish-subscribe protocol tailored for constrained IoT hardware[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a subfield of AI?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Machine Learning, Robotics, and NLP are all integral branches of Artificial Intelligence[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a supervised learning algorithm?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Decision Tree is a supervised machine learning algorithm trained on labeled target data[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a common type of E-Commerce model?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: B2C, C2B, and C2C are all recognized, standard e-commerce models[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a B2C E-Commerce website?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Amazon functions prominently as a Business-to-Consumer online retail platform[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a multimedia authoring tool?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Adobe Flash was historically designed as a multimedia authoring and animation development suite[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: In relational databases, what does the 'A' in ACID transaction properties stand for?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In ACID properties, 'A' stands for Atomicity, ensuring a transaction completes entirely or not at all.

questions.questionText: In C++, which OOP principle allows private data members to be hidden from direct unauthorized external modification?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data with functions and prevents arbitrary external access through private visibility[cite: 2].

questions.questionText: Which SQL Data Definition Language (DDL) command deletes an entire table along with its structural schema?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: DROP TABLE deletes both the schema and all stored table records permanently[cite: 1, 2].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a network layer hardware device that interconnects two separate networks and routes packets using logical addresses?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Routers operate at Layer 3 (Network Layer) and determine optimum packet delivery paths based on IP addressing[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: In relational database normalization, Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) requires that for every functional dependency X -> Y:
questions.optionA: Y must be a prime attribute
questions.optionB: X must be a super key
questions.optionC: X must be a foreign key
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: BCNF imposes that for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, X must strictly be a superkey.

questions.questionText: What is the process of loading the operating system kernel into main memory during system startup called?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Booting loads the initialization code and kernel into RAM when the computer power is switched on.

questions.questionText: In C++, an inline function member defined inside a class body is:
questions.optionA: Automatically treated as inline by default
questions.optionC: Required to use the explicit keyword 'inline'
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Any member function whose body is defined within the class declaration is treated by the compiler as inline by default[cite: 2].

questions.questionText: In an undirected simple graph with V vertices, what is the maximum possible number of edges?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A complete undirected graph with V vertices contains V * (V - 1) / 2 distinct edges.

questions.questionText: Which operating system CPU scheduling algorithm allocates equal slices of CPU time (time quantum) to processes in circular order?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Round Robin (RR) schedules processes using time slices (quanta) in a circular FIFO queue.

questions.questionText: In standard SQL, which wild-card character represents zero, one, or multiple characters in a LIKE pattern match?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The percent sign `%` in SQL matches any sequence of zero, one, or multiple characters.

questions.questionText: Which memory architecture is fastest in terms of data access time for a microprocessor core?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: L1 cache is integrated directly within the CPU core and has the lowest latency of all memory levels.

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct regarding the destructor of a class in C++?
questions.optionA: It can accept parameters for overloaded cleanup
questions.optionB: It has no return type and cannot take any parameters
questions.optionC: A class can define multiple overloaded destructors
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A destructor takes no arguments, returns no value, and cannot be overloaded[cite: 2].

questions.questionText: What is the binary 1's complement of the binary byte 10110010?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Inverting each bit in 10110010 gives 01001101.

questions.questionText: Which data structure is used in Breadth First Search (BFS) graph traversal?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: BFS uses a FIFO queue to discover and visit graph vertices level by level.

questions.questionText: Which standard network port number is assigned for default unencrypted HTTP traffic?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Port 80 is the default TCP port dedicated to unencrypted HTTP web communication.

questions.questionText: In SQL, what is the default behavior of the join operator if no condition is provided (e.g., SELECT * FROM A, B;)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Listing tables separated by commas without a WHERE clause results in a Cartesian Cross Product.

questions.questionText: In operating system process states, moving a process from Running state to Ready state is caused by:
questions.optionB: Time quantum expiration or higher-priority interrupt
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A running process is moved back to the ready queue when its allocated time slice expires or a priority preemption occurs.

questions.questionText: Which C++ keyword explicitly allows a non-member function access to private and protected members of a class?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The `friend` declaration allows an outside function or class access to private and protected class members[cite: 2].

questions.questionText: An Ethernet local area network (IEEE 802.3) employs which medium access control protocol?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Legacy shared Ethernet networks use Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection (CSMA/CD).

questions.questionText: What is the prefix expression corresponding to the infix expression: (A - B) * C ?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: (A - B) converted to prefix is `- A B`; multiplying with C gives `* - A B C`.

questions.questionText: A deadlocked state in operating systems occurs only when which set of conditions holds simultaneously?
questions.optionA: Mutual exclusion, Hold and wait, No preemption, Circular wait
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The four Coffman conditions necessary for deadlock are Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, and Circular Wait.

questions.questionText: Which wireless network standard defines Wi-Fi communication?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: IEEE 802.11 is the internationally recognized engineering standard defining Wi-Fi wireless networking[cite: 3].
